paragraphs: Mar Shmuel Mari. It appears that he was an exilarch and that his servants were licentious. A fetal sac came before him. He said, “This is forty-one days old,” and calculated from the day of immersion, but it was only forty days. He said, “That man had intercourse during her menstrual impurity.” He bound him, and he confessed: Niddah 25b. The mortar in Mar Shmuel's household: Eruvin 102a. The son of Mar Shmuel ordered thirteen thousand zuz to be given to Rav—it should read Rava—from the income. Rava sent the matter to Rav Yosef: Nedarim 55a. R' Yaakov, Rav Nahman's father, was his scribe. Rav Nahman bar Yitzhak brought him from the sun to the shade. Rav Pappa came to his house: Menahot 34a. He came to his house and did not eat, because of the servants' licentiousness: Beitzah 14b. Rav Pappa said: someone spoke against Mar Shmuel, and a reed fell from the roof and pierced the pouch of his brain. The Gemara says, “A Torah scholar is different, for the Holy One, blessed be He, exacts payment for his honor.” Rava led Mar Shmuel along and expounded: there, 21b.
